input.task: What is the price of the Aurora Desk Lamp?

provenance: PR #46 R1 (MEDIUM). `plan-lint-refuses-a-document-root-extract` grades the PRE-execution refusal: one `stub_plan`, the gap note goes to the planner, the stub returns the same plan, and the no-progress rule (`new_steps == steps`) ends the run — which is why its `replans` is 0. ADR-024's Consequences paragraph attributed that 0 to the OTHER branch, a mid-run adoption refusal, and no case in the PR reached `adopt()` with a document-root target at all: the rule was stated for a path nothing exercised. This is that path. The first plan only looks — `observe` on the catalogue list, the M32 drill-down (ADR-020) — and the replan it earns comes back with the root target. `adopt()` lints the spliced plan of record and refuses it, and mid-run that ends the run instead of replanning, because the drill-down WAS the replan. The two cases now cover both branches of the same clause and disagree about nothing: this one's `replans: 0` is the mid-run rule (a refused adoption is never counted as progress), that one's is the no-progress rule.

triage.watched_red: cannot fail before the thing it refuses exists, so watched red by ablation (ADR-009's method): `DOC_ROOT_ROLES` emptied, everything else untouched. checks {status: false, recovery: false, replans: false, trace_actions: false, answer_null: true}, got status `failure:locate`, budgets.actions 4, replans 1, tiers ['role'], reason "step 4 (extract): relocation after locate failure: retargeting as {'text': 'Nimbus Shop — Catalogue'}; ResolveError: no tier resolved {'text': 'Nimbus Shop — Catalogue'}" — the adopted plan ran, the root target failed to locate, and the ladder spent its rung on the page title. Restored, green.
triage.note: structural assertions only, for the reason `observe-drilldown-replan-is-linted` gives (PR #34 R13): `trace_actions` pins that the run got as far as the `observe` and stopped there — the refused plan's `extract` never ran — and `replans: 0` that the refusal was not counted as progress. A reason-string assertion would pass on any of the drill-down's four refusal exits. The task is deliberately non-aggregate, so the only clause that can produce this refusal is ADR-024's.
